units.text: This guide is for engineers who own a feature flag in the Orbit platform.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide

units.text: It explains how a flag goes from off to fully on, and what has to be true before each step.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide

units.text: It does not cover experiments, which follow their own process.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide

units.text: Each section below names the condition that must hold before the flag moves on.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide

units.text: Questions about the guide go to the platform team.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide

units.text: A rollout moves through three stages: internal, canary and general availability.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages

units.text: In the internal stage the flag is on only for staff accounts, so problems reach colleagues before they reach customers.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages

units.text: The internal stage usually lasts one working day, but the guide sets no minimum for it.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages

units.text: Canary then exposes a small share of real traffic to the change.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages

units.text: General availability turns the flag on for everyone, in steps of 25%, 50% and 100%.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages

units.text: Each stage is recorded in the rollout tool, which keeps the history of who moved the flag and when.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Rollout stages

units.text: During canary the flag is on for 5% of requests, chosen at random per request rather than per user.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Canary

units.text: It must stay at that level for at least 30 minutes, so that the metrics cover a full traffic cycle of the slowest endpoint.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Canary

units.text: The owner does not raise the percentage by hand during this time, because a manual change restarts the measurement window.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Canary

units.text: Short canaries are the most common reason a bad flag reaches general availability.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Canary

units.text: A flag advances from canary to general availability only when the automated metrics check passes.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary

units.text: The metrics check compares the error rate and p95 latency of flagged requests with the same requests over the previous 7 days.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary

units.text: If the check fails, the flag stays in canary and the owner investigates before trying again.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary

units.text: The rollout tool runs the check automatically at the end of the canary window.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Advancing from canary

units.text: Every flag must have a kill switch that turns it off within 1 minute.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch

units.text: The kill switch is tested in staging before the flag enters canary, and the test is recorded in the rollout tool.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch

units.text: A flag without a tested kill switch cannot enter canary.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch

units.text: Anyone on the owning team may use the kill switch without asking for approval.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch

units.text: Turning a flag off is always safe; turning it back on starts the rollout again from the internal stage.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Kill switch

units.text: While the flag ramps up, the owner watches the error dashboard and pages the on-call engineer if errors rise.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability

units.text: The dashboard shows flagged and unflagged requests side by side, so a difference between them points at the flag rather than at the platform.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability

units.text: The owner keeps watching until the flag has been at 100% for one hour.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Monitoring during general availability

units.text: A flag that has been fully on for 30 days is removed from the code.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Flag cleanup

units.text: The owner opens a cleanup ticket when the flag reaches 100%, and the ticket links to the rollout record.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Flag cleanup

units.text: Flags that miss the deadline are listed in the weekly stale-flag report.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Flag cleanup

units.text: Old flags make the code harder to read and slow down every later rollout.
units.topic: Feature flag rollout guide › Flag cleanup
